Rent a GPU for AI (2026): Cloud GPU and RunPod Pricing

# Rent a GPU for AI: cloud GPU prices from 13 providers, and the card your model needs

An RTX 4090 rents from $0.33 an hour, a data-centre H100 from $2.50. Cloud GPU prices from 13 providers, the card your model needs, and what the rate hides.

Updated 3 November 2026 · 15 min read · estimates are labelled as estimates

The short answer

An RTX 4090 rents from $0.33 an hour on home PCs, or $0.89 in a data centre, where an H100 starts at $2.50 (PCIe) or $3.49 (SXM). The same card can cost 4.6 times as much from one provider as from another, and the cheapest hour is often not the cheapest token.

The cheapest hours on a 24 or 32 GB card

 SaladCloud or RunPod Community An RTX 4090 for $0.33 or $0.34 an hour. Both are machines run by someone else; SaladCloud's are home PCs that can drop without warning. On Vast.ai, another marketplace, each host sets its own price. 

A 24 to 48 GB card in a data centre

 RunPod and Hyperstack An RTX 4090 for $0.89 or an L40S for $1.09 on RunPod; an RTX A6000 for $0.50 on Hyperstack. 

A 70B model on one GPU

 A100 80 GB on Hyperstack $1.35 an hour holds Llama 3.3 70B at 4-bit (about 45.8 GB). On paper the MI300X (AMD) at $2.59 an hour is cheaper per token. 

One H100, no contract

 Hyperstack and Jarvislabs The PCIe card from $2.50 (Hyperstack), the faster SXM from $3.49 (Jarvislabs, in India). Of the big clouds, AWS rents a single H100 SXM for $6.88 and Azure a single H100 NVL for $6.98; Google only eight at a time. 

The cheapest H100 hour, for public data

 RunPod Community $1.99 an hour for an H100 PCIe, its list price, on a third-party host's machine. Stock comes and goes, and someone else runs the machine, so keep it to public models and test data. 

Requests that come in bursts

 Modal or RunPod Serverless Billed per second of work, and almost nothing while idle (a short idle window bills). An H100 on Modal is $3.95 an hour of work, for the GPU alone. 

A big cloud, and you can choose which

 AWS The cheapest of the three for an H100 at $6.88, as a single GPU. New accounts start with a GPU quota of zero, so ask for an increase first. 

On this page

## The cheapest cloud GPU for your model

Start from what you want to run. The tool works out the memory a model needs with the same formula as the rest of this site, keeps every card that holds it with room to spare, and prices each one at its cheapest listed provider. It opens on Llama 3.3 70B at 4-bit with 8k of context; change any of it.

Which cloud GPU runs your model

Listed prices read 19 October 2026, on demand, before tax; stock comes and goes. Speeds are one-user ceilings worked out from memory bandwidth, not measurements.

 Llama 3.3 70B 70.6B 

Runs on one consumer card

 Hours a month 100 h 100 

Llama 3.3 70B at 4-bit with 8k of context needs about 45.8 GB. The cheapest single GPU that holds it: A100 80 GB at $1.35 an hour on Hyperstack, $135 for 100 hours a month. Cheapest per token: the MI300X, about $7.94 per million tokens at 91 tokens a second.

| Split across GPUs (speed depends on the link between them) | | | | |
| RTX A6000 2 GPUs 48 GB · RunPod Community · third-party host | $0.66 | $66 | split | - |
| RTX 3090 4 GPUs 24 GB · RunPod Community · third-party host | $0.88 | $88 | split | - |

"Sold as 8" means that provider rents the card only in 8-GPU machines, so the hour is for all eight. Per million tokens is one user at a time; a server batching many users gets far more from the same hour. * Past 100 tokens a second the formula overstates speed, so these rows count 100 tokens a second for the cost per token: a best case.

## Cloud GPU prices by card

The lowest on-demand price per GPU for each card, read from each provider on 19 October 2026. "Any host" includes marketplaces and home PCs; "run by the provider" leaves them out; the last price column is the cheapest of AWS, Google Cloud and Azure. Serverless prices, billed per second of work, are in the provider table below.

- The same card, very different prices. An H100 SXM is listed from $2.69 (RunPod Community, third-party host) to $12.29 (Azure, 8-GPU machines): 4.6 times as much for the same GPU.
- Vast.ai is named without prices. It is a marketplace where each host sets its own price, and its terms do not allow its prices in a comparison like this one without a written agreement. Check its live prices.
- Lium figures are the cheapest listing you could rent when we read its public node list: Secure machines only, not Spot ones that can be reclaimed, and one GPU where the machine rents them singly. Cards with nothing free at that moment are left out. Lium also publishes "reference" prices and what renters paid over 30 days; both are often below any listing, so we use neither.
- Prices move, and stock comes and goes. Nebius raised its H100 from $3.85 to $4.50 an hour on 1 October 2026. At RunPod and the marketplaces a listed card can be gone a minute later.
- Cheaper with strings attached. Interruptible machines cost less: Nebius's preemptible H100 from $0.79 an hour, Google's Flex-start H100 at $4.79. So do commitments: Hyperstack's reserved H100 SXM from $2.72, CoreWeave up to 60% off. This page compares on-demand prices only.
- Two providers publish no usable price list. TensorDoc
